section2_limits.text: What this does not establish. Every reading at every stage was produced by one family of language model. Where two readings agree, that is one voice heard twice, not two independent witnesses, and agreement in this record must never be taken as confirmation. No report by a human scholar is among the listed files. Whether any reader consulted anything beyond the witnesses named in section 8 is not tested by this record.
The readings were not all of one kind. Reading A examined %s of the %s groups of units, Reading B %s and Reading C %s.

No reconciling reading exists for this book: where first readings differ, this record shows them side by side, then whatever the adjudicator ruled. Each review between revision rounds is one reader's report, not a pair.

The first readings read the entries as they stood after the second revision round, not as they stand now. The entry's words quoted in section 3 are the final words; a reading's words may answer an earlier wording. The revision logs of section 4 show what moved.

section4_limits.text: Limit. The fourth and fifth revision rounds left no revision log in the list of landed files, so the words of their changes are not printed here. What is known of them is what the readers who followed them counted. The review of the fourth revision counted %s entries and %s elements changed. The second audit counted %s entries and %s elements changed by the fifth revision and %s entries byte-identical.

section8.text: A limit on the statements above. The book's own files state no licence term for the World English Bible: they name it and say that its attribution terms travel with any quotation, and they do not say what those terms are. The witness text files themselves state no terms: a search of the three of them for the words licence, public domain, Creative Commons or copyright found %s occurrences. The terms should be confirmed against each witness's own distribution before this record is published. This record makes no claim on any witness beyond quotation for the purpose of showing what was argued from it.
